children.name: Amphizoa insolens
children.description: Amphizoa insolens is a species of aquatic beetles.

children.name: Amphizoa lecontei
children.description: Amphizoa lecontei is a species of aquatic beetle. Adults have a body length of between 11.5 and 16 millimeters. Its elytron has a distinct carina on fifth interval. The species is found in western North America, especially in the Rocky Mountains. Its common name is "Trout-stream beetle". Its synonym is Amphizoa carinata.

children.name: Amphizoa sinica
children.description:
Amphizoa sinica is a species of beetle in the Amphizoidae family. The length of its body is between 11 and 13.5 millimeters. Its metasternal process is depressed, with the lateral margin raised. It lives in the northeastern province of Jilin in China and in North Korea.
It was first described in 1991 by Yu Peiyu and Nigel Stork.

children.name: Amphizoa striata
children.description: Amphizoa striata is a species of trout-stream beetle in the family Amphizoidae. It is found in North America. It is between 13 and 15 millimeters long. Its front tarsi have a well-developed groove on the posterior surface and grooves bearing a fringe of long hair-like setae. It lives in British Columbia, Oregon, and Washington.
